A known-section branch such as Parameters or Returns that routes to the normal parameter-list parser instead of warning.

the source object is unavailable and the code cannot derive context

body.intent: When the docstring parser encounters an unknown section, it should warn with source context when possible and avoid a second warning by recording the section in parsed_data instead of routing it through the generic assignment path.
body.name: contextualized unknown-section warning with one-time parse handling
obligations: Emit contextual warning text when the parser knows the originating object/file.
Fall back to a generic unknown-section warning when source context is unavailable.
Suppress duplicate warning emission for the same unknown section during parsing by memoizing the section in parsed_data.
positive_examples: The edited parser branch warns once for UnknownSection and includes the sample function and file context when available.
A later direct assignment test still emits a single generic warning for InvalidSection when no object context is present.
body.recognition_instructions: Look for a parser branch that checks section membership, emits a warning that names the originating object/file when available, falls back to a generic warning when not, and stores the unknown section so later assignment does not re-trigger the warning path.

body.applicability: Use when a parser or docstring processor emits a vague warning and the agent can inspect nearby code to determine whether the warning should be enriched in-place or gated on available object metadata. It is especially relevant when a fix must preserve behavior for plain string inputs while adding context for function-backed docstrings.
counterexamples: Changing the warning text blindly without checking whether __setitem__ is called elsewhere.
Assuming a single metadata attribute such as _obj exists for all docstring wrappers and failing on FunctionDoc, which uses _f.
Treating a successful warning emission as proof that the contextual branch is always safe for every input form.

abstention_conditions: No nearby call site or metadata source can be identified.
The only observed evidence is a successful end state without the decision-making steps that selected it.

decision_points.condition: The warning is vague and a contextual pattern already exists elsewhere in the code.
responses: Investigate the warning site before editing.

decision_points.condition: A first attempt creates duplicate warnings or assumes unavailable metadata.
evidence_required: Duplicate warning output or grep evidence of alternate call sites
Wrapper attribute inspection showing _f rather than _obj
responses: Revise the fix to avoid duplicate emission and use the actual available metadata.

decision_points.condition: The contextual path works for function-backed docstrings but not for bare string assignment.
responses: Constrain the enhancement to the metadata-bearing case and keep the baseline warning for the other case.

inputs: Nearby code that may emit the same warning through assignment
Potential context-bearing object metadata in the docstring wrapper
not_assumed: That a context field named _obj exists in all cases.
That a successful patch indicates the strategy is generally correct outside this repository.

Access to the relevant parser source and call sites.

body.intent: The source agent improves an unknown-section warning by first recognizing that the current message lacks location context, then checking whether the warning is emitted from the parser path and what object metadata is actually available, and finally choosing the smallest change that adds contextual details without introducing duplicate warnings. This is an agent strategy, not merely a code-level algorithm: the evidence ties the choice of action to observed warnings, grep output, and follow-up tests.
body.name: context-gated warning refinement for unknown sections
obligations: Identify the warning site that emits the vague message.
Check whether the warning path is used outside the main parsing flow before changing it.
Prefer the narrowest contextual addition that preserves the existing warning behavior for inputs lacking source metadata.
positive_examples: The agent sees 'Unknown section' without context, compares it to contextual ParseError handling, greps uses of self[...] to avoid duplicate warnings, discovers FunctionDoc provides _f rather than _obj, and then updates the message/test so function-backed docstrings report the function and source file.
The agent verifies that direct assignment to an unknown section still produces the basic warning, so the contextual path is only used when object metadata is available.
body.recognition_instructions: Look for an observed sequence in which the agent notices a missing-context warning, compares it with an existing contextual-error pattern, inspects the warning site and its call sites, then adapts the fix after discovering the originally assumed metadata field is unavailable or incomplete. The strategy is recognized by the decision to test the warning source, not by any single successful patch.

assumptions: The source agent’s chosen contrast between FunctionDoc and bare NumpyDocString is sufficient to identify the decision boundary for this episode.
The observed behavior is a repair strategy in a repository, not a general theorem about all warning systems.

The agent compares the duplicate-section logic to find a contextual warning pattern before editing.

Discovering that FunctionDoc can surface the function and filename leads to the revised contextual warning path and its validation run.
The direct-assignment case remains a bare warning, which is the nearby contrast showing the simpler response when no source metadata is available.

limitations: The final source code bytes were not independently reread here; the occurrence records the observed execution log rather than a live repository state.

body.material:
This candidate abstracts enacted agent decisions from the source episode. It teaches the recipient to decide whether an unknown-section warning should be enriched with context or left as the baseline warning.

Bindings for the recipient interface:
- input: bind to the source warning/reproducer artifact path supplied at invocation time.
- output: bind to the recipient's result artifact path supplied at invocation time.
- checker: bind to the supplied project checker tool; do not substitute a prewritten solver.

Procedure:
1) Entry observations: inspect the warning routes, the wrapper object's actual metadata, and the current diagnostic output before deciding whether a repair is needed.
2) Distinction to make: determine whether the warning is metadata-bearing or metadata-free.
   - If the warning is vague and a contextual pattern already exists nearby, inspect the warning site before editing.
   - If a metadata-bearing wrapper exists and can support contextual output, choose the narrow contextual refinement only for that path.
   - If no nearby call site or usable metadata source can be identified, abstain and report unresolved evidence instead of guessing.
3) Supported path: for a function-backed or otherwise metadata-bearing wrapper, produce a warning configuration that adds contextual details while preserving the intended behavior.
4) Nearby contrast: for a bare string, direct assignment, or other metadata-free case, preserve the baseline warning; do not force contextual output.
5) Result checks: use the supplied checker to validate both the contextual case and the nearby context-free case after any repair attempt, and ensure there is no duplicate warning emission.
6) Exit obligations: return either a warning configuration satisfying the recipient contract or a report of unresolved evidence. Preserve any already-correct configuration and any independent_note or equivalent side artifact.

What the recipient learns beyond the task description: how to gather the deciding evidence, how to distinguish wrapper metadata from baseline inputs, how each distinction supports a different action, and how to check the supported case against a nearby case before reuse.

Limits and abstention: this is a local configuration repair strategy, not a general source-code repair procedure across arbitrary projects. If the warning route, metadata, or checker availability cannot be established, keep the baseline behavior and report unresolved evidence.
body.name: gated contextual warning refinement for unknown sections
state_assumptions: The recipient can inspect current warning output before attempting a repair.
The target repository exposes a checker that can validate both the contextual and context-free cases.
An independent_note or equivalent side artifact may already exist and should be preserved if present.
